title: rosa canina subvar. hispidula
intro: Rosa canina subvar. hispidula, commonly known as the dwarf dog rose, is a subspecies of the Rosa canina species, which is a type of rose bush native to Europe and Western Asia. The dwarf dog rose is valued for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to protect against chronic diseases such as heart disease and cancer. The therapeutic actions of the dwarf dog rose are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which may exert anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects. The bioactive constituents of the dwarf dog rose also include vitamin C, which is essential for immune function and collagen production, making it a valuable plant for promoting overall health and well-being.
